issues.legal_issue: The limitation period for making a land-acquisition declaration is measured by its publication in the official gazette, not by the later completion of all required modes of publication.
material_facts: The preliminary acquisition notice was last published in the official gazette on 6 August 1992.
The declaration was made on 3 August 1993 and published in the official gazette on 5 August 1993, within one year of the preliminary notice’s final publication.

The declaration was subsequently published in newspapers and public notice was given in the locality on 28 August 1993, after the one-year period measured from the preliminary notice’s final publication.
The landowners argued that the later completion of the declaration’s publications made it time-barred.
issues.conclusion: The declaration was not barred by limitation because its publication in the official gazette occurred within one year of the final publication of the preliminary notice. The later publications did not determine the limitation period. The High Court was wrong to treat the date the declaration was made as the relevant date, but its rejection of the challenge was correct.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 4(1) and 6(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the limitation period runs from the last date of publication of the preliminary notification, and the declaration is complete for this purpose when it is published in the official gazette. The last-date definition in Section 6(2), introduced for purposes referred to thereafter, does not govern the limitation for making a declaration under Section 6(1); it is relevant to subsequent steps, including the period for making an award under Section 11-A. The Court followed Krishi Utpadan Mandi Samiti v. Makrand Singh, (1995) 2 SCC 497, and noted that State of Haryana v. Raghubir Dayal, (1995) 1 SCC 133, supported its construction. It held that Jagrup Singh v. State of Rajasthan, AIR 1993 Rajasthan 157, did not correctly state the law.

rule.if: land_acquisition_limitation_appeal and preliminary_notice_final_publication and declaration_gazette_publication_within_deadline and later_publication_after_deadline

predicates.land_acquisition_limitation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging whether a land-acquisition declaration was made within the applicable time limit.
predicates.preliminary_notice_final_publication: The required publications of the preliminary acquisition notice were completed, establishing the start of the limitation period.
predicates.declaration_gazette_publication_within_d: The declaration was published in the official gazette within the applicable time limit measured from the preliminary notice’s final publication.
predicates.later_publication_after_deadline: Other required publication steps for the declaration were completed only after that time limit had expired.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges the timing of a land-acquisition declaration, the declaration is timely if it was published in the official gazette within the applicable deadline, even if other required publication steps were completed later.
